title: Labeled chip-firing on the line with an odd number of chips: evidence for two open conjectures
statement: For labeled chip-firing on Z from n = 2m + 1 chips at the origin (Hopkins-McConville-Propp 2017): the maximal number of inversions of a stable outcome is m for n <= 11 (their Conjecture 26 was verified for n <= 9); the exact probabilities of the sorted outcome under random protocols 1 and 2 are 1/3, 1/5, 0.2501/0.2512, 0.3118/0.3147, 0.3305/0.3314 for n = 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and Monte Carlo estimates up to m = 80 are within 0.006 of 1/3, consistent with their Conjecture 27 (limit 1/3).
resolves: nothing; extends the evidence for Hopkins-McConville-Propp Conjectures 26 and 27
verified: check_line.py: exact outcome sets and maximal inversions for n <= 9 and exact rational sorting probabilities for n <= 9 under protocols 1 and 2 (pure Python).
zline.cpp / exactp.cpp: n = 11 (6,520,201 states, 819 outcomes, maximal inversion 5; P(sorted) 0.3305156511 and 0.3314399523).
mc.cpp: 20,000-run Monte Carlo per point for m = 2..80.
unresolved: protocol 3 (uniform stabilization sequence) was not computed
nonclaims: no proof is claimed; this dossier is evidence only
smallest_decisive_test: An odd n with a stable outcome of more than (n - 1)/2 inversions, or sorting probabilities converging away from 1/3.
